title: Boom-type platforms: the 11 metre threshold by state
moduleTitle: Optional add-on: high-risk work and platform licences
audience: Workers and supervisors who may be asked to work at height or on a platform. Optional add-on, taken alongside the main courses.
learningOutcomes: Apply the boom-length rule for each state that this lesson covers.
Explain why Queensland's platform definition excludes platforms under 11 metres.

instruction.heading: Where the 11 metre rule applies
instruction.body: Several states set the boom-type platform licence by boom length. SafeWork NSW's licence page states a WP licence where the boom is 11 metres or more. WorkSafe Tasmania states that a WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and that no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (page last updated 1 December 2023). WorkSafe WA's WP licence class page applies the same 11 metre boom length (published 11 August 2026, last updated 13 August 2026).

instruction.heading: Northern Territory and ACT
instruction.body: The Northern Territory's elevating work platform bulletin states the 11 metre threshold for the WP licence (no date shown). The ACT high risk work licence page lists a WP licence where the boom is 11 metres or more; the page shows a fee period and no publication date.

instruction.heading: Queensland's platform definition
instruction.body: Queensland's boom-type platform page says a WP licence is needed to operate a boom type elevating platform, and that platforms under 11 metres are not included in that definition (no date shown).

instruction.heading: What is not confirmed
instruction.body: How boom length is measured is not confirmed by an official source in this add-on. Confirm the measurement rule with the state regulator before relying on a length figure.

procedure: Measure the boom length of the platform.
Find the state rule for that boom length on the regulator's page.
Record the page date and confirm the measurement rule before work starts.

workedExamples.situation: A 9 metre boom-type platform is offered for a job in Tasmania, and the supervisor asks whether the operator needs a WP licence.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What does the Tasmanian rule in this lesson say?
workedExamples.reasoning: The WorkSafe Tasmania page says no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres, so on that rule a 9 metre boom is outside the WP licence. Confirm the boom length and the current page before work.

commonErrors.error: Using the 11 metre figure for every state.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the rule for the state where the work is done; this lesson lists only the states named.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Boom length decides the licence position in several states. Measure the boom and check the state rule before work. This add-on does not grant a licence.

qualityStandard: Learner gives the boom-length rule for each state named, with the page date.
documentationEvidence: Boom length measured, state rule checked, page date recorded.
summary: Several states use an 11 metre boom-length rule.
Queensland's definition excludes platforms under 11 metres.
Measurement rules are not confirmed by an official source here.

knowledgeChecks.question: Under the Tasmanian rule summarised in this lesson, when is a WP licence needed?
options: Where the boom is 11 metres or more
Only where the boom is under 11 metres
